rules.text: At both case points the crop alternated between corn and soybeans every year from 2008 to 2023, so this is the rotation already in use.

rules.citation: Manski, Socolar et al., "Diversified crop rotations mitigate agricultural losses from dry weather" (manuscript read at https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10554940, Nov 14 2026)
rules.text: In a model of over 2.2 million field-years in Illinois and Minnesota, moving from a 2-crop to a 3-crop rotation lowered the modeled risk of low corn yields in dry weather. In nearly all Illinois counties, over 90% of fields showed reduced risk.

rules.citation: Manski, Socolar et al., "Diversified crop rotations mitigate agricultural losses from dry weather" (manuscript read at https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10554940, Nov 14 2026)
rules.text: In neighboring Logan County, Illinois, the median reduction was about 5 percentage points in the probability of low corn yields in dry conditions.
The study measures how many crops a rotation has, not a specific third crop. Choosing a small grain such as wheat is our assumption and needs local review.

rules.citation: CropWatch, University of Nebraska-Lincoln, "More diverse crop rotations improve yield, yield stability and soil health" (https://cropwatch.unl.edu/2021/more-diverse-crop-rotations-improve-yield-yield-stability-and-soil-health, read Nov 14 2026)
rules.text: In a long-term Nebraska trial, fertilized corn yielded 29% more in two-year rotations and up to 48% more in four-year rotations than continuous corn. These comparisons are against continuous cropping, not against corn-soybean.

rules.citation: Manski, Socolar et al., "Diversified crop rotations mitigate agricultural losses from dry weather" (manuscript read at https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10554940, Nov 14 2026)
rules.text: Across 11 long-term experiments, diverse rotations reduced corn yield losses by 14 to 90% in drought years in half of them, as reported by this study citing earlier work.
The Nebraska trial is a single site under no-till, and the clover was a winter cover crop in only one of four years. Grain sorghum is not grown in the observed McLean fields.
